title: ReactWise runs two ways: a UI for chemists, and an API for the instruments/data infrastructures.
summary: Read the latest news and updates from ReactWise about AI-driven chemistry and process optimization.
body_markdown:
ReactWise runs two ways: a UI for chemists, and an API for the instruments/data infrastructures.


The interface is where you design plates, get experimental recommendations, simulate outcomes, and generate insights through visualizations by looking at what a campaign is telling you. It's built for a chemist making decisions in the lab, and most people spend most of their time there.


The application programming interface (API) handles all integrations..


It connects directly to hardware - liquid handlers, flow setups, PAT instruments, OPC UA servers - and to the infrastructure where your data already lives, including databases and electronic lab notebooks. Recommendations go out to the equipment, results come back in, and nobody is exporting a CSV to move data between two systems that should already be talking.


That's the difference between a tool you use and a tool that's part of your workflow. If you're running closed-loop experimentation, or just want campaign data landing in the right place without someone retyping it, the API is where the platform gets interesting.


Both routes are covered by the same security posture: ISO 27001 certified and SOC 2 Type II.


If you're already running ReactWise and haven't looked at the API suite or are just curous, it's worth 20 minutes.


Message me and I’ll tell you more.
